Roofing in Sunnyvale, Texas

Sunnyvale is a small town of large lots in eastern Dallas County, with its own permit process for re-roofs. One free call connects you with an independent roofing company that serves Sunnyvale.

Call (469) 649-7066 Sunnyvale re-roof permits
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Sunnyvale

Four hamlets and a one-acre rule

Roofing in Sunnyvale, TX looks different from roofing in the denser suburbs around it, and the reason goes back to 1953.

That year, four rural communities in eastern Dallas County, Long Creek, New Hope, Hattersville and Tripp, joined to form the Town of Sunnyvale. The name came from a contest at the Tripp-Long Creek school; the students' first choice, Sunnyville, was already taken. The new town allowed only single-family houses on one-acre lots, which set the pattern for much of the town. Sunnyvale had 2,693 residents in 2000 and 5,130 in 2010.

Where lots are big, there are often more trees close to houses, longer driveways, and often a barn, shop or carport with a roof of its own. A roofer quoting in Sunnyvale may be asked about all of them at once.

Sunnyvale re-roof permits and the roofing inspection

Apply online

The town requires every permit application to be completed online through its portal. Its residential fee schedule lists a roof and re-roof permit.

The inspector looks up close

Sunnyvale's inspection list has a roofing stage: underlayment, insulation, crickets, flashing and the finished roof.

Current codes and fees

The town builds to the 2021 International Codes with local amendments. A new fee ordinance took effect September 8, 2025, so ask for current amounts.

The town's fee list also carries a contractor registration line for general contractors. Ask your roofer whether it is set up with Sunnyvale and who will apply for the permit.

Where the 2015 tornado began

On the evening of December 26, 2015, a tornado formed in Sunnyvale and tracked northeast into Garland and Rowlett. In town it caused extensive damage to the Plantation RV park. By the time it crossed Interstate 30 in Garland it had reached EF-4 strength, and the National Weather Service in Fort Worth named it for all three places: the Sunnyvale-Garland-Rowlett tornado.

Storms like that are rare. Hail and straight-line wind come far more often, and on a one-acre lot the risk includes limbs from mature trees landing on the roof. After a storm, check the roof from the ground, photograph any damage, and call the insurer before permanent repairs.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before hiring a roofer in Sunnyvale

  • Will you apply for the Town of Sunnyvale permit and tell me when the roofing inspection passes?
  • Where does my roof need crickets or new flashing, and is that in the written price?
  • Do you also quote barns, shops or carports, and in what material?
  • Which trees should I have trimmed back from the roof by a tree service before you start?
  • Who writes your liability policy, and will the insurer send me the certificate?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

How a call from Sunnyvale works

DFW Expert Roofers is a phone line, not a contractor. Calling it is free.

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

Hail on the house and the shop roof, or a limb across the eaves? Call and describe it. The roofer serving Sunnyvale that you are put through to sees it in person and writes up its estimate.

Sunnyvale roofing questions

How do I find roofing contractors in Sunnyvale TX?

Look for a company that will pull the Town of Sunnyvale permit and is set up with the town to do so; the town's fee list includes a contractor registration line. Ask for its liability insurance certificate from the insurer and a written contract. If you call the DFW Expert Roofers line, the automated assistant connects you with an independent local roofer that serves Sunnyvale. The line itself does no roofing. How to check a roofer.

Is there a roofing permit in Sunnyvale?

Yes. The Town of Sunnyvale's residential fee schedule includes a roof and re-roof permit, and all permit applications are made online through the town's portal. The fee schedule was replaced by a new ordinance in September 2025, so ask the town for the current amount. The roofer normally applies and schedules the inspection.

What does Sunnyvale check when it inspects a roof?

The town's inspection list includes a roofing stage covering underlayment, insulation, crickets, flashing and the finished roof. Crickets are the small ridged sections that steer water around a chimney or other obstruction. Because the inspector looks at those details, ask the roofer to leave time in the schedule for the inspection and to tell you when it has passed.

Did the 2015 tornado hit Sunnyvale?

Yes. The National Weather Service calls the December 26, 2015 tornado the Sunnyvale-Garland-Rowlett tornado because it began in Sunnyvale before moving northeast. It badly damaged an RV park in town on its way into Garland, where it reached EF-4 strength. Sunnyvale also gets the ordinary hail and wind of every North Texas spring. See storm damage roof repair.
